items.definition: The most widespread and fertile soil, formed by rivers depositing silt across the northern plains
Also called regur, made from weathered lava rock and ideal for cotton in the Deccan plateau
Soil that turns reddish because iron diffuses in crystalline and metamorphic rock
Soil formed by intense leaching in areas of high rainfall and alternating wet and dry spells
Sandy, saline and low in humus and moisture, found mainly in western Rajasthan
Soil of hilly and mountainous regions whose texture varies with the parent rock

items.subject: Rice
items.value: A kharif crop sown with the onset of the monsoon and needing high temperature with heavy rainfall

items.subject: Wheat
items.value: A rabi crop sown in October to December and harvested in April to June

items.subject: Watermelon
items.value: A zaid crop grown in the short summer season between rabi and kharif

items.subject: Sugarcane
items.value: A crop that takes almost a full year to mature and grows in both north and south India

items.subject: Cotton
items.value: A crop grown on black soil and the main raw material of the textile industry

items.subject: Jute
items.value: Known as the golden fibre, it needs well-drained fertile soil in flood plains

items.subject: Tea
items.value: A plantation crop needing a warm, moist, frost-free climate and deep fertile soil

items.definition: The cropping season sown with the onset of the monsoon around June and harvested in September to October.
The cropping season sown in October to December and harvested in April to June.
A short season during the summer months between rabi and kharif.
Shifting cultivation in which forest is cleared and burnt, farmed briefly, then left fallow to recover soil fertility.

items.subject: Magnetite
items.value: The finest quality iron ore, containing up to seventy per cent iron

items.subject: Haematite
items.value: The most important industrial iron ore, containing fifty to sixty per cent iron

items.subject: Manganese
items.value: A mineral chiefly used in the manufacture of steel and ferro-manganese alloys

items.subject: Bauxite
items.value: The principal ore from which aluminium is obtained

items.subject: Limestone
items.value: A sedimentary mineral that is the basic raw material of the cement industry

items.subject: Copper
items.value: A malleable, ductile metal used in electrical cables, electronics and chemical industries

items.definition: Everything available in our environment that can be used to satisfy our needs, provided it is technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally acceptable.
Development that takes place without damaging the environment and without compromising the needs of future generations.
A declaration signed at the 1992 Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit to combat environmental damage, poverty and disease through global cooperation.
The removal of the top layer of soil by water, wind or human activity such as deforestation and overgrazing.
Erosion in which running water cuts deep channels called gullies through clayey soil, making the land bad or ravine.
Ploughing along the contour lines of a slope so that furrows slow down the flow of water and reduce erosion.
Rows of trees planted across a landscape to break the wind and check soil erosion in coastal and dry regions.
The international body that classifies species as normal, endangered, vulnerable, rare or extinct.
A species in danger of extinction, with its population having fallen to a critically low level.
A species found only in a particular area, isolated by natural or geographical barriers.
A programme from 1988 onward in which village communities are entrusted with the protection and management of degraded forest land.
A Himalayan movement against deforestation in which villagers, notably women, hugged trees to prevent them being felled.
A situation in which water availability is insufficient to meet the demands of a region, in quantity or in quality.
A project across a river that serves several objectives together, such as irrigation, electricity, flood control, navigation and fish breeding.
Collecting and storing rainwater, for example through rooftop systems, khadins, johads, tanks or bamboo drip systems.
A diversion channel used in the hilly areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu to carry water to villages.
The production of goods in large quantities after processing raw materials into more valuable products.
An industry that uses agricultural produce as its raw material, such as cotton textiles, jute or sugar.
Harm caused when hot water from factories and thermal plants is drained into rivers and ponds before cooling.
A road linking major cities across states, built and maintained by the central government.
A mode of transport that moves crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas in liquid or gaseous form, with low running costs.
The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur gas pipeline, the longest gas pipeline in India.
A railway along the western coast that overcame difficult terrain of rivers, mountains and coastal plains.
A navigable route on rivers, canals, backwaters or creeks, the cheapest mode of transport for heavy goods.
